why: I checked each line's evidence against the repository. Line 1 PASS names wrong builds (a hard-coded '0' fill, ignoring width) and says why they fail: padLeft('42',5,'0') and the default-space call padLeft('42',5) catch them. Line 2 PASS names a build that cuts to width "like truncate does", which padLeft('123456',5,'0') catches. Line 3 FAIL names a concrete wrong build: it adds only a padLeft section, so it meets the line, but the README stays incomplete. That is real: index.js exports slugify and README.md has only capitalize and truncate sections. Line 4 PASS names a build that rewrites truncate, which test/strutil.test.js catches. That suite really does cover capitalize, slugify and truncate under "node --test". The cited files, functions and scripts all exist. The only claim I couldn't check is "Node v22.23 here can require() ESM", which is about the environment, not the repository.
